messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU_ECC_ERRORS spike on cluster-prod-gpu-03 — 6 events in 5m. Trigger: gpu.ecc.errors > 5 over 5m. Paging SRE-oncall.
Alex P: grabbing this. seeing ECC errors + a couple nodes with VRAM util ~98%. Thanks bot. :eyes:
Sam R: I’m looking at telemetry now — VRAM and temp look correlated on node gpu-03. Thermal throttling events around the same time.
Maria G: quick handoff — @Alex P you oncall? I can help with blast radius if you want me to stay on.
Alex P: yes oncall. Trying to confirm customer impact. Any 5xx from serving?
ops-bot: service:inference-api returning elevated latencies for model:open-l1-variant between 02:05–02:18 UTC. 95p latency up ~2.3x. No large increase in error rate.
Sam R: logs show occasional OOMs on one pod pinned to gpu-03, k8s evicted it twice — `OOMKilled` in pod logs. Might be mem leak or bad scheduling.
Alex P: mitigation plan: (1) drain node gpu-03, (2) restart pods on other nodes, (3) suppress noisy ECC alerts with a rate limit and longer window while we investigate. Any objections?
Maria G: +1 to drain. Prefer cordon -> evict -> monitor rather than immediate delete. Use `kubectl drain gpu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` with caution.
Sam R: agreeing. Also propose we split alerts by metric: keep ECC critical if >0 persist for 10m; turn VRAM util into a warning at 85% (5m) and critical at 95% (3m) tied to OOMs. Current rule was 90%/1m which is too noisy.
Alex P: doing cordon now. `kubectl cordon gpu-03` -> cordoned.
ops-bot: node gpu-03 marked unschedulable.
Alex P: starting drain (eviction in progress). Will watch evictions and reschedules.
Sam R: while drain runs I'll open a quick PR for alert tuning and a new dashboard panel showing per-GPU: VRAM used, temp, ECC count, and kernel thermal events. Will link.
Maria G: also add an alert that fires on node_drain_in_progress for >10m without completing — had that overnight once and it sat.
Alex P: eviction finished. Pods evicted and recreated on gpu-01/gpu-02. Inference latency recovering toward baseline.
ops-bot: latency back to normal 02:28 UTC. No customer 5xx spike.
Sam R: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/alerts/pulls/234 — changes:
```
- gpu_vram_high:
    expr: avg_over_time(gpu_vram_utilization[5m]) > 0.9
    for: 1m
+ gpu_vram_warn:
    expr: avg_over_time(gpu_vram_utilization[5m]) > 0.85
    for: 5m
+ gpu_vram_crit:
    expr: avg_over_time(gpu_vram_utilization[5m]) > 0.95
    for: 3m
+ gpu_ecc_crit:
    expr: increase(gpu_ecc_error_count[10m]) > 0
    for: 10m
```
Sam R: also added mute window in pagerduty for repeated ECC alerts on same node (rate limit 2 alerts / 30m).
Maria G: for post-incident followups: assign infra to run vendor diagnostics on gpu-03, file support ticket (serial: GPU-03-AXY), and schedule a Grafana dashboard review to add thermal anomaly panel.
Alex P: summarized impact: nodes impacted: gpu-03; customer visible latency increase ~2.3x for ~20m, no successful request errors at scale, a few OOMKilled pods. Mitigation: drain node and rebalanced pods.
Maria G: action items: [ ] PR merge for alerts and dashboard (Sam) [ ] vendor diag + RMA if needed (infra) [ ] add node drain monitor alert (Alex) [ ] postmortem draft (Maria)
Sam R: merging PR after one more review; tagging @Maria G for review.
ops-bot: Incident closed by Alex P at 02:40 UTC — automated summary posted to incidents channel.
Alex P: thumbs. I'll write a short postmortem and include tuning rationale for VRAM vs ECC separation. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
